cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / Biltmore Fashion Park — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / Biltmore Fashion Park opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / Roosevelt Filed — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / Roosevelt Filed opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear SchoolSpring Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Permanent Building Substitute - 2026-27 School Year- 1 opening- .875 FTE opportunity with SchoolSpring at SchoolSpring.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Middle School Paraeducator - Special Education — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear SchoolSpring Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Middle School Paraeducator - Special Education opportunity with SchoolSpring at SchoolSpring.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear Charter Oak Recruitment Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the High School Social Studies, Haven Charter High School opportunity with Charter Oak Recruitment at Charter Oak Recruitment.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Extension Administrative Support Specialist in Craig 633368 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Oklahoma State University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Extension Administrative Support Specialist in Craig 633368 opportunity with Oklahoma State University at Oklahoma State University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Future Opening: Apprentice — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Surface Experts Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Future Opening: Apprentice opportunity with Surface Experts at Surface Experts.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Orientation Trainer - 1st Shift — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pilgrim's Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Orientation Trainer - 1st Shift opportunity with Pilgrim's at Pilgrim's.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Engineer I, Drug Product Development
jobs.description: The Role We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Individual, to work in a team developing Moderna’s sterile drug product processes and products that enable clinical and future commercial supply. The primary role for this position will be to support product concept development including process development and scale-up work, container development and conditions of use studies. The incumbent will support the development of aseptic fill/finish unit operations and drug product packaging through the development and use of scale-down models, process characterization studies etc. Applicants should have relevant pharmaceutical sciences related experience with various aspects of drug product development. The applicant should have exceptional ability to plan, execute and report, to communicate and collaborate, and requires strong attention to detail while working in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary environment. Here’s What You’ll Do Conduct studies to support scale-up of drug product manufacturing (e.g. freeze/thaw, mixing, filling, filtration, lyophilization, etc). Conduct studies to support the drug product container / package development (e.g. shipping stress studies, label permeation studies, leachable & extractable studies, etc.). Develop protocols to evaluate the compatibility of the drug product with processing materials, container closure components, and sterilization processes. Provide support to drug product development activities executed in collaboration with Moderna’s Pilot organization, including toxicology fills stability fill operations. Plan, organize and execute experiments (using DoE where possible) – prepare study protocols and summarize the development results with presentations and study reports. Communicate and collaborate with various groups such as analytical development to execute experiments and compile data. Support manufacturing with studies for process trouble-shooting and investigations. Maintain an up-to-date ELN with good documentation practices Closely collaborate with multiple groups to generate innovative solutions to challenging formulation and process problems. Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications) Education Qualifications - Masters or Bachelor’s Degree in on one of the following fields: Chemical Engineering, Biochemical or Packaging Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or any related or sub-disciplines of the above. Relevant Experience: 0 – 2 years post Master’s Degree or 0 – 4 years post Bachelor’s Degree. Exceptional laboratory skills with ability to work efficiently and productively in a highly dynamic environment. Knowledge of statistical design of experiments (DoE) and analysis Knowledge of nucleic acid chemistry and biology is a plus Preferred: Experience in BioPharma, BioPharmaceutical, Pharmaceutical, or Biotechnology industry Preferred: Experience with nanoparticle formulation technology Preferred: Knowledge of GMP compliance Pay & Benefits At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between. Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown Savings and investments to help you plan for the future Location-specific perks and extras The salary range for this role is $63,200.00 - $100,900.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance. cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineer I, Drug Product Development — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Moderna Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineer I, Drug Product Development opportunity with Moderna at Moderna.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: BIM Designer & Coordinator
jobs.description: About the Team Industrial Compute is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. Working alongside our capital partners, engineering teams, and construction organizations, we design and deliver large-scale, mission-critical compute campuses that power the next generation of AI. Our Design organization brings together engineering, construction, and digital design to ensure facilities are coordinated, constructible, and optimized from the earliest planning phases through deployment. About the Role We are seeking a BIM Designer & Coordinator to support the planning and design of large-scale industrial and mission-critical facilities. In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain multidisciplinary BIM models across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural disciplines, enabling early design validation, constructability reviews, equipment planning, and cross-functional coordination. You will partner closely with internal engineering teams, external design consultants, contractors, and project stakeholders to produce coordinated BIM deliverables that improve design quality, reduce project risk, and support efficient execution across Industrial Compute's global infrastructure portfolio. Key Responsibilities: - Develop and maintain conceptual and schematic BIM models for large-scale industrial and MEP-intensive facilities. - Coordinate BIM models across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural disciplines. - Create and maintain federated models used for design reviews, spatial coordination, constructability analysis, and clash detection. - Model major building systems including equipment layouts, utility corridors, electrical rooms, mechanical rooms, structural framing, site infrastructure, and architectural constraints. - Coordinate equipment clearances, maintenance access, routing zones, shafts, risers, utility entrances, and major MEP pathways. - Translate engineering sketches, basis-of-design documents, equipment lists, one-line diagrams, and planning documentation into coordinated BIM models. - Support early design activities including test-fit studies, routing evaluations, phasing plans, utility coordination, and design option analysis. - Maintain BIM standards including model organization, file naming conventions, worksets, shared coordinates, view templates, and model health. - Support multidisciplinary coordination using Navisworks, Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Revizto, or similar collaboration platforms. - Prepare model views, coordination packages, exports, and documentation for design reviews and stakeholder meetings. - Support model-based quantity takeoffs, equipment tracking, asset information, room data, and design progress reporting. - Review consultant and contractor BIM deliverables for quality, coordination, completeness, and compliance with project BIM standards. - Help maintain digital design assets that support planning, design development, construction coordination, and operational handoff. Discipline Focus Areas CIVIL BIM DESIGNER - Develop site models including grading concepts, access roads, utility corridors, stormwater systems, underground duct banks, and civil infrastructure. - Coordinate civil infrastructure with building footprints, substations, generators, cooling equipment, underground utilities, and site constraints. - Experience with Civil 3D, ArcGIS, Revit Site, and utility modeling is preferred. ELECTRICAL BIM DESIGNER - Develop conceptual and schematic models for substations, switchgear, transformers, generators, UPS systems, cable tray, busway, duct banks, grounding systems, and major power distribution infrastructure. - Coordinate electrical equipment clearances, cable routing, service entrances, and access requirements with architectural, structural, mechanical, and civil disciplines. - Experience with Revit Electrical, AutoCAD, Navisworks, and interpreting one-line diagrams is preferred. MECHANICAL BIM DESIGNER - Develop models for mechanical equipment, chilled water systems, hydronic piping, airside systems, ductwork, pumps, chillers, CRAH/CRAC units, heat exchangers, tanks, and central utility plants. - Coordinate mechanical routing, maintenance access, pipe racks, structural supports, overhead zones, and major penetrations. - Experience with Revit Mechanical, Navisworks, and industrial piping and duct coordination is preferred. ARCHITECTURAL / STRUCTURAL BIM DESIGNER - Develop architectural and structural models including building shells, floor plans, slabs, structural steel, foundations, equipment pads, platforms, stairs, and access areas. - Coordinate architectural and structural constraints with MEP systems, utility entrances, equipment placement, and code-required clearances. - Experience with Revit Architecture, Revit Structure, AutoCAD, and Navisworks is preferred. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related technical field. - 3+ years of BIM modeling, BIM coordination, drafting, or design technology experience. - Experience developing 3D models using Revit, AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Navisworks, Inventor, SolidWorks, or comparable BIM/CAD platforms. - Experience supporting multidisciplinary coordination for complex industrial, infrastructure, or building projects. - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, equipment layouts, design narratives, diagrams, and consultant deliverables. - Strong understanding of BIM standards, model organization, file management, and coordination workflows. Preferred Skills - Experience supporting large-scale industrial, data center, manufacturing, utility, or other mission-critical infrastructure projects. - Experience developing conceptual and schematic design models in addition to construction documentation. - Strong understanding of multidisciplinary MEP coordination, equipment clearances, routing zones, and constructability considerations. - Experience with Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Navisworks, Revizto, Bluebeam, Civil 3D, ArcGIS, Dynamo, Python, or Autodesk Platform Services. - Experience supporting model automation, asset management, data extraction, quantity takeoffs, and design reporting. - Experience coordinating with internal engineering organizations, external consultants, contractors, and owner representatives. - Excellent communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural engineering teams. About the Role We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager, Data Center Infrastructure: Owner Furnished Equipment to lead sourcing strategy for the critical infrastructure systems that power Industrial Compute campuses. This role will develop commercial strategies, negotiate strategic supplier agreements, and manage relationships across engineering, construction, manufacturing, and infrastructure partners responsible for delivering mission-critical facilities. You will work closely with Infrastructure Delivery, Capacity Planning, Engineering, Finance, Construction, and external suppliers to ensure Industrial Compute has the capacity, supplier relationships, and commercial frameworks required to support rapid global expansion. The ideal candidate has experience sourcing major infrastructure systems for hyperscale data centers, mission-critical facilities, industrial construction, semiconductor manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or similarly complex capital projects. Key Responsibilities - Develop long-term sourcing strategies for data center infrastructure systems supporting Industrial Compute. - Lead strategic supplier selection, RFx processes, commercial negotiations, and contract execution for major infrastructure programs. - Build and maintain executive relationships with key suppliers, manufacturers, EPC firms, integrators, and infrastructure vendors. - Partner with Infrastructure Delivery and Engineering to align sourcing strategies with project schedules, technical requirements, and deployment priorities. - Collaborate with Capacity Planning to ensure supplier capacity aligns with long-term infrastructure roadmaps. - Evaluate supplier capabilities across manufacturing capacity, execution quality, financial health, delivery performance, and operational maturity. - Identify and mitigate supply chain risks through supplier diversification, long-term agreements, alternative sourcing strategies, and capacity reservations. - Monitor global market conditions, manufacturing trends, commodity impacts, geopolitical risks, and supplier ecosystems that may affect infrastructure delivery. - Develop supplier scorecards and performance metrics across quality, cost, schedule, responsiveness, safety, and execution. - Support executive sourcing decisions through financial analysis, market intelligence, scenario planning, and supplier benchmarking. - Partner with Legal and Finance to structure scalable commercial agreements that support Industrial Compute's long-term infrastructure strategy. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Operations, Finance, or a related field. - 8+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supplier management, or infrastructure supply chain management. - Experience sourcing major infrastructure systems, industrial equipment, mission-critical facilities, or large capital projects. - Proven experience negotiating complex commercial agreements with strategic suppliers. - Strong understanding of supplier qualification, contract strategy, supplier performance management, and sourcing governance. - Experience partnering with engineering, construction, finance, legal, and operations organizations. - Excellent analytical, financial modeling, negotiation, and executive communication skills. Applying engineering principles, you will troubleshoot and resolve equipment-related issues. Ensure proper housekeeping and maintain cleanliness (6S) of the working area. Timely report/ escalate any concerns (work-related or personal). Meet daily production schedule and performance expectation. Able to take on additional tasks or responsibilities when required. jobs.description: About the Team At DoorDash we’re building the industry’s most scalable and reliable delivery network to support our three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers. TPMs on our Engineering teams provide fundamental support to the underlying technology services as well as the engineers building these services. It’s no simple task, but it wouldn’t be interesting if it was! About the Role New Verticals is building the future of local commerce at DoorDash: making the city shoppable by helping consumers get groceries, convenience items, retail products, and more with the quality, speed, and affordability they expect. The organization operates at significant scale and is expanding beyond the core marketplace into new fulfillment models and merchant-facing products. Our work spans the consumer shopping experience, catalog and inventory, pricing and affordability, fulfillment, merchant integrations, and the platform capabilities that connect them. Our team is looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager to lead complex, high-impact programs across New Verticals Engineering. This role sits at the intersection of product, platform, and operations, helping translate ambitious business bets into executable technical strategies. You will work across Grocery, Convenience, Retail, DashMart Fulfillment Services, and emerging Merchant Services initiatives, where success requires navigating deeply interconnected systems, evolving product requirements, and dependencies across multiple DoorDash organizations. You will bring strong technical judgment, create clarity in ambiguous spaces, identify risks before they become blockers, and drive programs from strategy through launch and scale. You will report into the centralized Technical Program Management team in Engineering. You must be located in either the San Francisco Bay Area or Seattle. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Drive New Verticals' Most Strategic Programs - You will partner closely with Engineering and Product leadership, Strategy & Operations, and cross-functional teams to turn New Verticals' strategy into executable technical programs. The portfolio spans growing Grocery and Convenience, scaling Retail selection and shopping experiences, evolving DashMart Fulfillment Services, and building new Merchant Services capabilities. Lead Complex Cross-Organization Execution - New Verticals depends on capabilities across consumer experience, catalog and inventory, pricing and promotions, logistics, merchant integrations, ads, and platform infrastructure. You will establish clear ownership and milestones, surface critical dependencies and tradeoffs, and drive alignment across teams when the path forward is not obvious. Bring Technical Depth and Systems Thinking - You will develop a deep understanding of the architecture, data flows, and operational systems behind New Verticals. You will engage in technical designs, identify scaling and reliability risks, understand how decisions in one part of the system affect the end-to-end customer and merchant experience, and help teams make pragmatic tradeoffs. Turn Ambiguity into Strategy and Action - Many of our hardest problems do not begin with a clean scope or a single owner. You will truth-seek across technical and business inputs, frame the problem, clarify the definition of success, develop a point of view on risks and options, and create an execution path that teams and leaders can align behind. Connect Engineering Execution to Business Outcomes - You will understand the customer, merchant, and economic outcomes behind the work and use that context to guide prioritization and execution. Whether the goal is improving speed and quality, expanding selection, making shopping easier, or improving cost to serve, you will help teams stay focused on the technical work that matters most to the business. We're excited about you because… You’re experienced in working with large-scale distributed systems, as well as client-side and platform teams, who own Tier 0 services serving external customers. You can speak to system architecture, scalability and reliability decisions, and design trade offs. You’re a strong leader with the ability to collaborate and build relationships across organizations, bridge gaps between teams, and successfully influence without authority. You have strong ownership, urgency, and drive. You are willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into the details to understand and drive your programs. You have excellent written & verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate with confidence, clarity, and focus. You can convey concepts and considerations to non-experts and experts alike. You’ve engaged with Engineering teams on product & platform development with a thorough understanding of software development processes and project planning. You are pragmatic and detailed in your approach and focus on progress, not perfection. Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree with experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering or other related discipline. 8+ years recent experience as a Technical Program Manager at a technology company. Experience in large-scale distributed systems and system architecture. Experience working with full-stack engineers and directly engaging on product development, with a thorough understanding of software development processes. Project planning and execution skills that include reviewing technical design documents, estimating, and scheduling. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 applications and AI tools. Competencies: Ability to identify business needs and translate them into effective HR systems and process solutions. Ability to work effectively in an international team environment , including across time zones and multicultural settings. Strong interpersonal skills , including the ability to remain composed when managing challenging client interactions and coaching others. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy. .

cold_email.subject: Interest in Sr Associate Human Resources — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sr Associate Human Resources opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin
